topology: PE1/PE2 carry BLUE AS100 on tagged Gi0/1.110 and RED AS200 on Gi0/1.120 over one shared physical link. Both tenants reuse client192.168.10.10, server192.168.20.10 and transit10.0.0.1/2. PE2 passive loopbacks198.51.100.110/32 and198.51.100.120/32 provide unique isolation controls. Practice begins with only PE2 BLUE configured as AS999.
implemented: Seventeenth ENARSI Layer3 Technologies entry with independent practice/completed documents, six-row addressing plan, staged instructions, executable reference/verification commands and current-origin/path/query permalinks. Simulation engine, UI layout, artwork and terminal are unchanged.

Named process TENANTS uses independent IPv4 VRF address families. Initial diagnosis requires three real PC-BLUE requests dropped No route in BLUE and three delivered replies in both RED host/server directions. BLUE has no peers or learned remote LAN routes while RED remains operational.

Repair removes only the incorrect PE2 BLUE family and recreates AS100 with its router ID, exact network statements, explicit passive LAN/loopback interfaces and active transit. RED family configuration and forwarding are preserved. VRF/process names are local labels; this lab uses consistent names for clarity.

Operational checks require two independently scoped peer pairs, forward/return internal D routes at AD90 and RIB15360, wide topology distance1966080 and RD1310720. CEF selects the correct VRF subinterface despite identical addresses. The global table must contain no tenant routes; static shortcuts, wrong tags, wrong bindings and missing advertised prefixes revoke live health.

Host traffic requires three accepted requests and parent-linked replies in all four tenant directions, with actual transmit/receive frames on correct physical tags and correct endpoint identities. HTTP requires two complete distinct200 service bodies at the same URL; a wrong tenant page cannot pass.

Isolation requires own-tenant loopback delivery, real No route cross-tenant failures in each VRF, successful explicitly scoped router probes and three actual global-table No route drops. Undefined-VRF errors, missing positive controls or successful probes in only one table cannot impersonate isolation.

Passive-transit exercise removes only BLUE adjacencies and learned routes while RED works. Missing-network exercise retains the BLUE peer and loopback while withdrawing its server /24. Access-binding exercise clears its IP but keeps BLUE router-originated core delivery available. Inbound-filter exercise keeps peers and the BLUE control route while rejecting only the BLUE service prefix. Each needs actual BLUE failure and positive controls followed by fresh restored four-way tenant traffic.

Per-attempt configuration/route epochs prevent stale packets and config-only toggles from earning troubleshooting history. Six live and eight historical checks yield practice0/14, original diagnosis1/14, repaired baseline10/14 and full14/14. Completed reference provides six live checks only; exported YAML retains earned stages while dropping runtime. Canonical config replay and saved reload rebuild independent families and routes.
scope: IPv4 VRF-Lite with named EIGRP, tagged subinterfaces, overlapping tenant identities, scoped route filtering and explicit per-interface passive policy. No new CLI commands or engine changes were required. No fresh CML capture, MPLS L3VPN forwarding, RD/route-target behavior, route leaking, default-interface policy inheritance, hardware timing equivalence or IPv6 VRF exercise is claimed.
